pages.text: Millions of families across England are set to benefit from a new one stop shop for flood advice as the Environment Agency marks the start of Flood Action Week, and the government has set an ambitious new target to improve flood protection for 200,000 properties. ‘ Flood Action Online ’ a one stop shop for flood advice has been unveiled, with a focus to help people understand their home’s flood risk and take practical action to reduce this.

It brings together clear, actionable guidance, including on how to find out if they are at risk of flooding and get flood warnings, while also gaining easy access to Met Office weather alerts during an incident. Homeowners can also identify practical changes, like property flood resilience measures, to become more resilient to flooding. To ensure the nation is more resilient to flooding, the government is investing £4.2 billion between last April and March 2029 to repair and replace existing defences and construct new ones, with hundreds of projects set to be completed.

The new target for 200,000 properties to benefit from this investment will deliver a total economic benefit of £27.9 billion in avoided damage as communities gain better protection and growth is delivered in every postcode. The announcement is part of the government’s wide-ranging actions to face the challenges of our changing climate and build a more resilient country: one that can withstand droughts and floods, which can occur at the same time, and other extreme weather events. It comes as a new Flood and Drought Resilience Taskforce meets for the first time this week, to strengthen the nation’s ability to plan for and respond to extreme weather.

The government spent £2.65 billion in its first two years on flood defences, with almost 62,000 properties better protected – exceeding the original target of 52,000. This investment has also stabilised the condition of existing assets after years of decline, with the percentage of assets at or above their required condition rising to 93% at the end of March 2026. Today, as Environment Agency teams across the country continue their work to ensure vital protections remain strong, the government has set a target for asset condition to rise further to 93.5% by March 2029.

This comes as the Environment Agency launches their annual campaign Flood Action Week aimed to encourage people to prepare for flooding by taking proactive steps such as knowing their flood risk, preparing a flood plan, and getting flood warnings. Caroline Douglass, Executive Director for Floods at the Environment Agency, said: Behind the scenes, the Environment Agency maintains 260 mobile pumps, including 17 ultra-high-volume pumps, along with 25 kilometres of temporary barriers ready to be deployed wherever they are needed. They also operate a 24/7 response to flooding emergencies, with 600 people on call at any one time and plans in place to escalate its response when needed. The Environment Agency also provides free flood warnings to help people prepare for flooding and reduce the impact it has on their lives.

pages.text: A new Flood and Drought Resilience Taskforce will be launched this week, to champion community voices and strengthen the nation’s ability to plan for and respond to extreme weather. This year alone, the nation has experienced the effects of our changing climate, with a wet winter followed by a long, hot summer bringing our third drought in five years and the driest July in almost two centuries, while a more intense and wetter winter is now anticipated.

The largest flood defence programme in English history is being delivered by the government, with at least £10.5 billion committed between 2024 and 2036 to protect homes, businesses, and critical infrastructure from the growing threat of flooding. Meeting for the first time this Wednesday (14 October 2026), the new Taskforce will bring Floods and Drought Minister Emma Hardy together with representatives from more than 50 organisations, including the Environment Agency, Met Office, Mayoral authorities, the Fire and Rescue Services, and the farming, water and insurance industry.

The group will share expertise, from understanding risks and assessing preparedness to supporting a longer-term resilience strategy for floods and drought, helping to protect communities and the economy. The voices of communities affected by both issues will be central to the new taskforce, through direct engagement and the inclusion of more community-based groups, so their lived experiences and insights inform future policy development. In this week’s meeting, the agenda will focus on assessing the nation’s preparedness for potential flooding this winter, which shows the nation is better prepared compared to last year, and how members have improved their response.

It will also discuss emerging learnings from the ongoing drought, and if improvements could be made to aid the nation’s resilience to both flooding and drought. The Flood and Drought Resilience Taskforce will complement the work of the National Drought Group, which will continue to play its vital role in coordinating and overseeing the operational response to drought. The new Taskforce will maintain strong links between the two, with the National Drought Group’s expertise and insights helping to inform its work on strategic resilience and preparedness.

The government has already taken swift action in response to the drought, by holding water companies to account to reduce leaks, supporting farmers with a £65 million funding boost to build resilience, and changing the rules to make building on-site reservoirs easier. In 2026/27, £1.4 billion is being spent on building and repairing flood defences, with every £1 invested in flood defences preventing around £8 in economic damage.
